chunks: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: Ibn al-Sarraj mentioned that he wrote to you asking you about a mutamatti' who did not have a sacrificial offering, and you replied to him in your letter: He should fast on the days of Mina; and if that escapes him, he should fast on the morning of al-Hasbah and two days after that.
He said: As for the days of Mina, they are days of eating and drinking; there is no fasting in them, and seven days when he returns to his family.

key_terms.أَيَّامَ مِنًى: the days spent at Mina during hajj rites
key_terms.الْحَصْبَةِ: the morning of al-Hasbah, a named point in the hajj schedule
key_terms.سَبْعَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the seven days to be fasted after returning home
key_terms.صِيَامَ: fasting as a substitute legal obligation here
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: the sacrificial offering required in this hajj context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a mutamatti' in hajj who cannot find the sacrificial offering and wants to fast instead?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the mutamatti' in hajj who cannot find a sacrificial offering. It clarifies that the days of Mina are not days of fasting, because they are days of eating and drinking, and indicates that the remaining fasts are to be observed upon returning to one's family.
